applies_why: Yes: the judge decides a pressed link by citing the single sentence's own wording as decisive instead of weighing the challenger's chain against the link's chain by footing.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: by footing, never verse by verse — read one way it forbids using a single verse's own wording to resolve a chain collision; read another it permits noting a sentence's wording as substantive support. I weighed those and took the first reading.
why: The judge says the challenger's analogy is footed yet treats the single sentence's own words as resolving the issue, which is the retired verse-by-verse stating test.
